summary: Judge member CPU at 1 core over the hour and 0.5 core over its idle minutes, counting the daemon and its replication workers; daemon_load keeps its 2-core bound as load_max_cores

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay change; the CPU minutes are process memory.

schema.detail: No table, index or migration change; the seat check reads the existing local observations.

compatibility.detail: st slo and st doctor show cpu over the hour and a new cpu/idle row, unknown (no-data, info) until the daemon has been up an hour with at least 10 idle minutes; the request-latency cpu row's windows are now closed minutes with cores null until known and measured_seconds gone. The replication worker posts its process CPU to /v1/internal/replication/worker-status every 10 seconds; an older daemon refuses that report and keeps working, and a newer daemon with an older worker reads its CPU as unknown.

downtime.detail: Normal restart on deploy; the minutes start empty after each restart, so both CPU targets read unknown for the first hour.

recovery.detail: Swapping back to an older build restores the single 2-core target; nothing is stored.
